name: cars_loading
issue_title: Cars keep loading indefinitely on the home screen
signals_note: Pinned deliberately. This case measures RANKING, so the signal set is held fixed; letting IssueSignalService vary would confound every before/after comparison in the phase baselines. Signal extraction is evaluated separately.
principle: This is a RETRIEVAL ground truth, not a diagnosis.
It answers: which files must a competent developer have open to
diagnose this issue? It deliberately does not name a root-cause
line, because pinpointing the defect is the LLM's job downstream.
Ranking within a tier is a soft ideal and is reported for
information only. The hard assertions are tier membership:
tier 1 belongs in the top 5, tier 2 in the top 10, and the
distractor list belongs outside the top 5.

tier_1.why: Owns the loading state machine. Starts in CarsLoading() and only leaves it when a LoadCars event is handled. 'Stuck loading' is by definition a defect in, or a failure to reach, this transition.
The Firestore fetch the issue body names explicitly. An awaited call that never resolves leaves the BLoC in CarsLoading forever.
The repository hop the issue body names explicitly; it forwards the data source future to the use case.
Renders the CircularProgressIndicator the user is looking at and consumes CarState via BlocBuilder. The reported symptom is observed here.
Declares CarsLoading / CarsLoaded / CarsError. Any state-identity or transition problem is visible here.

tier_2.why: The direct call site between the BLoC and the repository. It sits inside the exact chain the issue describes and cannot be skipped when tracing the await.
Wires the whole chain. A wrong registration lifetime (registerFactory vs singleton) plausibly yields a BLoC that never receives its event.
Where LoadCars() is dispatched into the BLoC. A missing or misplaced dispatch is the classic cause of a permanently-loading screen.
Declares the LoadCars event that drives the transition out of CarsLoading.
The contract for the repository hop. Real but thin: five lines of abstract signature, so low diagnostic value.

must_not_rank_top_5.why: Generated FlutterFire configuration. Mentions 'firebase' more than any other file and contains no logic that could hang. This is the canonical false positive for lexical scoring.
A data holder. Car.fromMap could throw, but that surfaces as CarsError, not as indefinite loading.
Renders a car that has already loaded. Cannot run before CarsLoaded is emitted.
Unrelated presentation widget. Matches the 'car' signal only through the substring in 'card'.
A different screen, reached only after a car is selected.
Navigation only; pushes the car list screen but owns no loading state.
